entry.title: RAG Without Vectors? Why PageIndex Might be the Architecture We’ve Been Missing

link.title: RAG Without Vectors? Why PageIndex Might be the Architecture We’ve Been Missing

entry.summary: In recent times, Large Language Models (LLMs) have become the go-to solution for answering user queries. However, the context window (the maximum amount of tokenized text a model can process at one time) has remained a fundamental architectural limit. While recent models support longer contexts, researchers have established that model performance deteriorates with growing context length.¹ This creates problems for LLMs to accurately interpret and reason over long, complex, domain-specific documents.

entry.summary: In our brains, neurons constantly filter huge amounts of sensory data, recognizing patterns and ignoring unnecessary information. This is exactly what artificial neural networks do, and it is accomplished through activation functions.

entry.title: Getting Active: The Math That Makes Neural Networks Learn

link.title: Getting Active: The Math That Makes Neural Networks Learn

entry.summary: In today’s world, “Neural network” must be the most commonly heard term on a daily basis. Neural networks are computational models inspired by the human brain, designed to recognize complex patterns and make decisions based on data (predicting outcomes or classify data etc.). They consist of layers of interconnected nodes (neurons) that process and transmit information. One of the key components that enable neural networks to learn and perform complex tasks is the activation function.
